cases.title: Panel: Show me again explains the change already made with a frame, and makes no second demonstration

rubric.reason: Turn 5 ran preview_frame and made no change; it said "Tab's pivot moved to the middle of its left edge, and Tab didn't move" with no values. It handed the rest back in one sentence: "Now Door's yours: say done when its pivot is in the middle of Door's left edge." The remark that the frame came back blank is not grounds to fail.

Every name the mentor used (Door, Tab, Anchor Point, Position, middle of the left edge, pivot at center now) matches the snapshot's focus, places and place_now and the anchor_demo result, and no time was invented.

Each turn is short and moves one idea, ending on something to do. Turn 1 ends on the choice. Turn 2 ends on the A then Shift+P ask with no slide sentence. Turns 3 and 5 are one or two sentences plus the pending action. Turn 4 reports the one demo and hands Door's move over in prose, ending on "Say done when it's there."

Turn 5 calls preview_frame and changes nothing, then explains only the one change already made: "Tab's pivot moved to the middle of its left edge, and Tab itself didn't move". It gives no values or field names, offers no second demo and hands back with "Now Door is yours: say done…" (the blank frame is not grounds to fail).

Every name and place the mentor uses comes from tool output: Door and Door's left edge from the snapshot proposal, "each one's pivot is at its center" from place_now, Tab's middle-left and time 0 from the anchor_demo result, and Anchor Point and Position as the real property names.

Each turn is short, moves one idea and ends with a task. Turn 1 is the intent question plus the Door fallback, ending on the choice. Turn 2 repeats the place back, gives the Anchor Point/Position sentence and ends on "press A, then Shift+P". Turn 3 asks for Tab's properties. Turn 4 reports the one demo and hands Door back. Turn 5 explains the change in two sentences and hands Door back again.

Turn 5 runs only preview_frame and makes no change. It explains the one change in plain words ('Tab's pivot moved to the middle of its left edge, and Tab itself didn't move') with no values or field names, then hands back the pending step ('Now Door's yours: say done…').

Every name used (Door, Tab, Anchor Point, Position, the middle of the left edge, center now) appears in the snapshot or demo results. Turn 4's 'its edges are in exactly the same place' follows from the identical layer_bounds in both preview_frame results.

Each turn moves one idea and ends on a learner action. Turn 1 is the intent question plus one fallback. Turn 2 has the repeat-back and the first sentence, then the A/Shift+P ask. Turns 3–5 are short and end on 'tell me when both show' or 'say done when its pivot is on the middle of its left edge'.
